verses.text: The people began to complain about their troubles, and the LORD heard them. When he heard it, he became angry, and fire from the LORD burned among them and destroyed some of the edges of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was called Taberah, which means burning, because fire from the LORD had burned among them.
The mixed crowd of foreigners among them began to crave other food, and the people of Israel started crying again. They said, "If only we had meat to eat!
We remember the fish we ate for free in Egypt, and the cucumbers, melons, leeks, onions, and garlic.
But now we have lost our appetite. We never see anything but this manna!"
The manna was like small coriander seeds and looked like pale yellow resin.
The people went around gathering it. They ground it in hand mills or crushed it with stones, then boiled it in pots or made it into flat loaves. It tasted like bread baked with olive oil.
At night, when the dew fell on the camp, the manna fell with it.
Moses heard all the families crying, each man at the door of his tent. The LORD became very angry, and Moses was upset.
Moses said to the LORD, "Why have you brought this trouble on me, your servant? What have I done to displease you, that you put the burden of all these people on me?
Did I give birth to all these people? Did I bring them into the world, that you tell me to carry them in my arms, like a nurse carries a baby, to the land you promised their ancestors?
Where can I get meat for all these people? They keep crying to me, 'Give us meat to eat!'
I cannot carry all these people by myself. The load is too heavy for me.
If this is how you are going to treat me, please kill me right now, if you care for me at all. Do not let me face my own ruin."
The LORD said to Moses, "Bring me seventy of Israel's leaders, men you know to be leaders and officials among the people. Bring them to the Tent of Meeting and have them stand there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the Spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will help you carry the burden of the people, so that you do not have to carry it alone.

Tell the people: Make yourselves holy and get ready for tomorrow, when you will eat meat. The LORD heard you crying, 'If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!' So now the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
You will not eat it for just one day, or two days, or five, or ten, or twenty days,
but for a whole month, until it comes out of your noses and you hate it. This is because you have rejected the LORD, who is among you, and have cried to him, saying, 'Why did we ever leave Egypt?'"
But Moses said, "Here I am among six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat to eat for a whole month!'
Would there be enough even if all the flocks and herds were killed for them? Would there be enough even if all the fish in the sea were caught for them?"
The LORD answered Moses, "Is my power too small? Now you will see whether what I say comes true or not."
So Moses went out and told the people what the LORD had said. He gathered seventy of their leaders and had them stand around the Tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to Moses. He took some of the Spirit that was on Moses and put it on the seventy leaders. When the Spirit came on them, they prophesied, but they did not do it again.
Two men, Eldad and Medad, had stayed in the camp. They were on the list of leaders, but they had not gone out to the Tent. Yet the Spirit came on them too, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' helper since he was young, spoke up. "Moses, my master, stop them!"
But Moses answered, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his Spirit on all of them!"
Then Moses and the leaders of Israel went back to the camp.
Then the LORD sent a wind that brought quails in from the sea. It brought them down all around the camp, about a day's walk in every direction, piled about a metre deep on the ground.
All that day and night, and all the next day, the people went out and gathered quails. No one gathered less than about two thousand litres. Then they spread them out all around the camp to dry.
But while the meat was still in their mouths, before they had even chewed it, the LORD became angry with the people and struck them with a terrible disease.
So that place was called Kibroth Hattaavah, which means graves of craving, because there they buried the people who had craved other food.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people travelled to Hazeroth, and they stayed there.
